title: Minimax estimation over inverse source classes

items.title: A one-coordinate projection risk bound
items.statement:
Let $r\ge0$ and $\tau>0$. In the one-dimensional Gaussian location experiment with parameter $\theta\in[-r,r]$, action space $\mathbb R$, observation density
$$p_{\theta,\tau}(y)=\frac{1}{\tau\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-\theta)^2}{2\tau^2}\right)$$
with respect to Lebesgue measure, and squared-error loss, let $M(r,\tau)$ be the minimax expected risk over all measurable deterministic or randomized estimators. Put $b=\min\{r,\tau\}$ and take the prior assigning mass $1/2$ to each of $-b$ and $b$. The better of the estimators $y\mapsto0$ and $y\mapsto y$ has worst-case risk $T(r,\tau)=\min\{r^2,\tau^2\}$, and this prior has Bayes risk at least $T(r,\tau)/\sqrt{2e}$, so $M(r,\tau)\ge T(r,\tau)/\sqrt{2e}$.
items.strategy: Use the equal two-point prior at the interval endpoints, compute its posterior variance exactly, lower-bound the resulting Gaussian integral, and compare with the risk of the two projection estimators.

references.title: Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, 2011 draft, §2.3, equations (2.26)–(2.30), and §4.6, Theorem 4.17 proof, printed pp. 29–30 and 111–113
Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, §2, equations (12)–(13), PDF pp. 3–4

items.axiom_use: The finite prior, Gaussian integration, and scalar minimax comparison are choice-free.

items.title: Cutoff risk and minimax RMS error over statistical ellipsoids
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix $\epsilon>0$, $Q\ge0$, a nonincreasing sequence $s_j>0$ with $s_j\to0$, and a nondecreasing sequence $a_j>0$. Observe $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ for $j\ge1$, where the $\xi_j$ are independent standard normal variables, and let the unknown parameter range over
$$\Theta_a(Q)=\left\{\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R):\sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\right\}.$$
Let $R_*(\epsilon)$ be the square root of the minimax expected squared $\ell^2$ error over all measurable deterministic or randomized estimators from the product Borel data space to $\ell^2$, and put
$$R_{\rm cut}(\epsilon)=\left[\inf_{D\in\mathbb N_0}\left\{\frac{Q^2}{a_{D+1}^2}+\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^{D}s_j^{-2}\right\}\right]^{1/2},\qquad\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}.$$
Then $R_*(\epsilon)\le R_{\rm cut}(\epsilon)\le2.2R_*(\epsilon)$.
items.strategy: The exact cutoff-risk formula gives the upper bound. For the lower bound, maximize the coordinatewise box-risk functional under the ellipsoid budget, choose its saturated coordinates as a prefix, bound a cutoff risk by twice this maximum, and use a finite product of endpoint priors with the one-coordinate lemma.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, §1, equations (3)–(9), and the complete proof in §2, PDF pp. 1–5
Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, 2011 draft, §§4.3–4.6, printed pp. 104–113

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the inverse sequence model and the exact-risk supplier. The finite endpoint prior and the lower-bound calculation use no additional choice.

items.title: Polynomial and exponential minimax estimation rates
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, $Q>0$, and $p,\kappa>0$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, the minimax RMS error over $\Theta_a(Q)$ has the following order-sharp rates: if $s_j\asymp j^{-p}$ and $a_j\asymp j^\kappa$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp\epsilon^{\kappa/(\kappa+p+1/2)}$; if $s_j\asymp e^{-pj}$ and $a_j\asymp j^\kappa$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{-\kappa}$; if $s_j\asymp j^{-p}$ and $a_j\asymp e^{\kappa j}$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp\epsilon[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{p+1/2}$; and if $s_j\asymp e^{-pj}$ and $a_j\asymp e^{\kappa j}$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp\epsilon^{\kappa/(p+\kappa)}$. Here $u_j\asymp v_j$ as $j\to\infty$ or $f(\epsilon)\asymp g(\epsilon)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ means the ratio is bounded above and below by positive constants on the indicated tail; the constants may depend on $Q,p,\kappa$ and the axis comparison constants.
items.strategy: Estimate the cutoff bias and cumulative variance in each polynomial or exponential regime, choose an integer cutoff at their order-balance, prove the matching lower bound by splitting cutoffs below and above that threshold, and transfer the result by the minimax comparison theorem.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, §3 and Table 1, PDF pp. 5–6
Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, 2011 draft, §4.5, Proposition 4.16, and §4.6, Theorem 4.17 proof, printed pp. 109–113

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the Gaussian sequence model and the minimax comparison theorem; the bias-variance balances are choice-free.

title: Minimax estimation over inverse source classes — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Sobolev ellipsoid rates in polynomial and exponential spectra
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, take $Q>0$ and Sobolev-type weights $a_j\asymp j$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse model. If the singular values satisfy $s_j\asymp j^{-1}$, the minimax RMS error is of order $\epsilon^{2/5}$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$; if instead $s_j\asymp e^{-j}$, it is of order $[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{-1}$. The comparison constants may depend on the fixed ellipsoid and axis constants.
items.strategy: Substitute p=kappa=1 into the polynomial-weight rows of the minimax-rate corollary and simplify the exponents.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, §3 and Table 1, PDF pp. 5–6

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the sequence model; the specialization is choice-free.

items.title: Analytic ellipsoid rates in polynomial and exponential spectra
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, take $Q>0$ and analytic-type weights $a_j\asymp e^j$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse model. If the singular values satisfy $s_j\asymp j^{-1}$, the minimax RMS error is of order $\epsilon[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{3/2}$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$; if instead $s_j\asymp e^{-j}$, it is of order $\epsilon^{1/2}$. The comparison constants may depend on the fixed ellipsoid and axis constants.
items.strategy: Substitute p=kappa=1 into the analytic-weight rows of the minimax-rate corollary and simplify the exponents.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, §3 and Table 1, PDF pp. 5–6

items.title: First-order power-source rates in polynomial and exponential spectra
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and let $Q=\rho>0$, $\nu=1$, and $K$ be a compact real infinite-rank operator. Over its minimum-norm power source ball $X_{1,\rho}(K)$, if $s_j\asymp j^{-1}$ then the minimax RMS error in the Gaussian sequence inverse model is of order $\epsilon^{2/5}$; if $s_j\asymp e^{-j}$ then it is of order $\epsilon^{1/2}$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. The constants may depend on $\rho$ and the fixed singular-value comparison constants.
items.strategy: Identify the source ball with the ellipsoid having weights a_j=s_j^{-1}, then apply the polynomial/polynomial and exponential/exponential rows of the minimax-rate corollary.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, Definition 2 and §3, Table 1, PDF pp. 2 and 5–6
